fields.sections.0.h: Apple Service Advertisements Appearing in iOS Settings App
fields.sections.2.h: Discontent Spreading Across Social Media and Communities
fields.sections.5.h: Possible Bug and Future Ad Expansion Prospects
fields.sections.0.ko: Apple has inserted banner-style advertisements promoting its products and services at the top of iOS Settings app. These ads expose users to paid services including iCloud+ storage, free trials of Apple Music and Apple TV, AppleCare+ extended warranty, and more. The most frustrating aspect for users is that there are almost no ways to remove these ads.
fields.sections.1.ko: To eliminate these ads, users must either wait until they automatically expire (which can take weeks to months) or subscribe to the relevant service. In most cases, there are no buttons to close the ads, and when they do exist, they often do not work, according to user reports. While the ads remain, the Settings app continuously displays a notification badge.
fields.sections.2.ko: Users are extensively complaining about Apple's action across social media such as Twitter and Reddit. One user expressed dissatisfaction comparable to what Microsoft introduced in the Start Menu, and other users have expressed strong resistance. In particular, complaints posts have surged in connection with recent iPhone launches.
fields.sections.3.ko: Historically, Apple has positioned itself as a premium company prioritizing user experience, but now repeatedly urging customers to purchase additional products contradicts this image. Especially when users see ads immediately on newly purchased iPhones after paying a substantial amount due to price increases, it can feel as though already paying customers are being exploited further.
fields.sections.4.ko: As growth in the smartphone market reaches a plateau, Apple is allocating increasingly larger portions to its services division. iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV, and AppleCare+ are all part of this strategy. This reflects a management decision to increase revenue in the services sector rather than limited hardware growth opportunities, but inevitably means users encounter more ads on their devices.
fields.sections.5.ko: Some ads, particularly iCloud+ ads, are reportedly displayed even to users already subscribed to those services, raising suggestions that these may be bugs. However, if Apple does not correct and maintains them, it would suggest intentional action. As Apple's services-strengthening policy continues, ads are expected to be introduced into additional features such as Visual Intelligence, so users will likely face increasing numbers of ads.
fields.caveat: The original text is primarily event reporting, and caution is needed in judging intent since Apple's official explanation of exactly when and by what criteria each ad is displayed is not included.
